main_text.p: Radix eft pars plantæ, terris infixa, ex femine primo nata, calidi humidiq; innati cum principibus vitalibus functionibus prima fedes.
Ex radice enata pars deferens alimentū fupra terram nonnihil assurgit : idem vero accipientes ex deferente funt Rami, vel his ἀναλογόυ quid : in quorum extremitatibus flores ac femina nafcuntur.
Plantæ funt cùm minores, tum majores.
Minor planta eft, cujus radix, pars deferens & ramulus, eft minor & imbecillior.
Caulis eft pars deferens, carnofa fere.
Plantæ caule crefcentes, funt herbæ atq; olera. Quorum variæ differentiæ ab eo tractandæ, qui doctrinam Plantarum perfequi velit.
Culmus eft pars deferens gracilior, longa & cava.
Plantæ hos obtinentes funt, frumenta & legumina.
Major planta eft, cujus radix & pars deferens majores, funt lignææ subftantiæ.
Lignum eft pars plantæ majoris, compacta maximè, duraq;.
Pars deferens plantæ majoris vocatur Caudex: ex quo rami majores & firmiores enafcuntur.
Ab his plantis excrementa rejiciuntur: vel profsus, ut liquores & refinæ; vel in fuperficiem caudicis & ramorum, ad muniendam plantam, ut Cortex.

page.notes: Catchword "Fru-" is a partial word at the lower right; it is shown here as a catchword and not repeated in the text. The left-margin note "Cortex." is a marginal word beside the line "ut"; it is placed where it stands. Long s rendered as plain s throughout. Some letters in the scan are faint (e.g., "pars" in the line beginning "Ex radice", "Plantæ hos obtinentes"), and the Greek word "ἀναλογόυ" reading is uncertain: it may be "ἀναλόγου" or similar, so treat it with caution. The marginal note "Cortex." sits beside the line "ut liquores" and may belong to the next line; its exact placement is uncertain. Ornamental initial marks ("s" in the page number) were read as the page number 52.
